_readme: Item modifiers ('Rift affixes') -- see the item-modifier system plan for the full design. PHASE C: real, droppable content, replacing Phase A2's five test-fixture-only placeholders (fiery_test/hardened_test/swift_test/vampiric_test/fortunate_test, all retired -- see git history for the placeholders' own descriptions of what shape each was exercising). Every modifier below is authored against a real combat hook: `effects[].type` is a ModifierEffectType member name (case-insensitive; see Domain/Combat/ModifierEffect.cs for what each one means and which of magnitude/threshold/damageType it reads). Magnitudes here are the UNSCALED base -- the actual number a fight reads is `base x TierMultiplier(itemTier) x RiftMultiplier(riftTier)`, applied once at ContentDatabase.ModifierEffects (see Domain/Content/ModifierMagnitude.cs). ONE EFFECT PER MODIFIER, ALWAYS -- ModifierEntryResolver rejects any entry authoring more than one (see its own comment on why). Phase C originally bundled 2-4 effects per family under one rollable id (a single Fiery roll granted both the burn AND the fire resistance); a later designer pass split every bundle into single-effect affixes so a roll always grants exactly one rule -- see each split-off entry's own description for which original family it came from. None of the magnitudes below are final balance -- they are deliberately round starting numbers for a designer to retune once real drops are played; see each entry's own description for the design call behind its shape.

modifiers.description: Burns on every landed hit. Elemental family: Fire, the damage half -- Emberguard is Fire's separate resistance affix; a Fiery item does not also resist fire the way the original bundled Fiery/Frosty/etc. modifiers used to.

Fire glances off the wearer rather than catching. Elemental family: Fire, the resistance half -- Fiery is Fire's separate on-hit-burn affix. Split off Fiery's old bundle so a roll grants one or the other, never both from a single slot.

Every hit carries a bite of frost. Elemental family: Ice, the damage half -- Permafrost is Ice's resistance affix and Frostbite is Ice's chill-proc affix, both split off this modifier's old three-effect bundle.

Frost does not bite the wearer back. Elemental family: Ice, the resistance half -- Frosty is Ice's separate on-hit-frost affix and Frostbite carries the old bundle's chill proc. Split off so each rule rolls on its own.

A lucky strike leaves the target chilled to the bone. Elemental family: Ice, the chill-proc half -- Frosty carries the on-hit damage and Permafrost carries the resistance; this used to ride along with both on one bundled Frosty roll, now it is its own affix.

Thorns answer every blow. Elemental family: Nature, the damage half -- Thornhide is Nature's resistance affix and Entangling is Nature's root-proc affix, both split off this modifier's old three-effect bundle.

The wearer's own hide grows thicker against green and growing things. Elemental family: Nature, the resistance half -- Sylvan is Nature's separate on-hit-thorn affix and Entangling carries the old bundle's root proc.

A lucky strike tangles the target in root and vine. Elemental family: Nature, the root-proc half -- Sylvan carries the on-hit damage and Thornhide carries the resistance; this used to ride along with both on one bundled Sylvan roll, now it is its own affix.
Every strike leaves a sting behind. Elemental family: Poison, the damage half -- Antivenom is Poison's separate resistance affix, split off this modifier's old two-effect bundle.

The wearer has long since built up a tolerance. Elemental family: Poison, the resistance half -- Venomous is Poison's separate on-hit-sting affix. Split off Venomous's old bundle so a roll grants one or the other, never both.
A sliver of the Rift rides every hit home. Elemental family: Arcane, the damage half -- Moonveil is Arcane's separate resistance affix, split off this modifier's old two-effect bundle.

A veil of the same Rift-sliver turns arcane harm aside. Elemental family: Arcane, the resistance half -- Astral is Arcane's separate on-hit affix. Split off Astral's old bundle so a roll grants one or the other, never both.

A brute, physical edge on every hit. Elemental family: Physical, the damage half -- Ironclad is Physical's resistance affix and Juggernaut is Physical's stagger-proc affix, both split off this modifier's old three-effect bundle (the one family with a third effect, since Physical had no typed-resistance twin worth calling out the way the other five elements do -- see Ironclad and Juggernaut's own descriptions).

Plating enough to turn aside a plain blow. Elemental family: Physical, the resistance half -- Hardened carries the on-hit damage and Juggernaut carries the old bundle's stagger proc; this used to ride along with both on one bundled Hardened roll, now it is its own affix.

Enough weight behind the swing to stagger whatever it lands on. Elemental family: Physical, the stagger-proc half -- Hardened carries the on-hit damage and Ironclad carries the resistance; this used to ride along with both on one bundled Hardened roll, now it is its own affix.

Every hit landed feeds the wearer a little of what it took. Base 15% at Ordinary tier 0 -- deliberately modest; Vampiric compounds with the healer role rather than replacing it, and the tier/rift curve is where a build actually gets scary. Already single-effect since Phase C; untouched by the affix split.

Armour plating a percentage curve cannot express. FlatPhysicalDamageReduction's base (3) is small on purpose at Ordinary/tier-0 -- it is a FLAT subtraction, so it matters far more against the many small hits of a swarm than against one boss-sized blow, which is the intended shape (a Stalwart wearer shrugs off chip damage, not a haymaker). Bulwark is this affix's split-off sibling -- the guard that gives less ground under pressure, split into its own roll so the two can no longer only ever be found together.

A guard that gives less ground under pressure. BreakShieldDepletionResistPercent (30) is forward-looking infrastructure -- no player combatant carries a BreakShield today, only some bosses/elites do, so this is inert on the wearer until a future fight puts one on the player's own side. Split off Stalwart's old bundle so a roll grants the flat mitigation or the shield-resist, never both.

Whatever the wearer finishes off does not go quietly -- the kill splashes onto whoever was standing next to it. The exact mechanism Trample already uses, so a Black Ram wearing this alongside his own talent gets two independent splashes off one kill rather than one doubled splash -- see OnKillSplashPercent's own comment on why that is deliberate, not a bug to fix later. Already single-effect since Phase C; untouched by the affix split.

The Prince favours whoever is wearing this, right now -- a flat, passive bonus to Prince's Favor for as long as it stays equipped, nothing stored and nothing that outlives taking it off. Base 3 at Ordinary/tier-0 sits alongside Shawn's own authored favour of 4: a meaningful nudge toward better drops, not a second currency to bank.

A deeper well of mana. Manaflow is this family's regen affix, Quickcast its mana-discount tempo affix, and Wardrune its mana-to-ward affix -- all four used to roll together as one bundled Runic modifier; split so each rolls on its own like every other affix.
A faster trickle of mana each turn. Runic's old bundle split four ways -- see Runic, Quickcast and Wardrune's own descriptions for the rest of the family.
A plain swing buys a cheaper follow-up cast. Runic's old bundle split four ways -- see Runic, Manaflow and Wardrune's own descriptions for the rest of the family.

Unspent mana becomes a ward at the top of the wearer's own turn. Deliberately the WEAK affix of the old Runic family (see FightTuning.RunicWardConversionRate's own comment) -- a safety net for mana a caster was going to leave on the table anyway, not a build-around tank strategy. Runic's old bundle split four ways -- see Runic, Manaflow and Quickcast's own descriptions for the rest of the family.

Phase D1's dodge family. A step too quick for a swing or a cast to reliably land -- Magnitude is a dodge RATING, not a direct percent, run through CombatMath.DodgePercentFrom's curve (100 * R / (R + 100), the same R/(R+100) shape as armour mitigation -- '100 dodge = 50% chance to dodge') before DamagePipeline.RollDodge rolls against it (see ModifierEffectType.DodgeRating for the full mechanics: zero damage, and every on-hit rider skipped with it). RENAMED from DodgeChancePercent, and the curve inserted, 2026-08-26: at a direct-percent reading, a maxed Swift item (base 12 x up to ~18.6x combined tier/rift scaling, ~223 raw) would have exceeded 100 outright -- a guaranteed, unavoidable dodge, which is exactly what the curve now prevents (that same ~223 rating instead reads as ~69%, per DamagePipeline's own hand-computed table). Base 12 at Ordinary/tier-0 curves to ~10.7%, close enough to the old flat 12% that it was left as-is rather than retuned. Already single-effect since Phase C; untouched by the affix split.
